title: A robotic-observatory night scheduler
description: Schedule one night for a small robotic telescope: astronomy constraints (airmass, twilight, Moon) through a typed UTC seam, a greedy baseline vs a seeded local search, 1000 Markov-cloud nights to price every promise, and a local model that proposes and explains while a deterministic validator decides.
outcome: You can build a constrained night scheduler whose every boundary is guarded: typed UTC instants into sky maths, an independent validator for any plan (including an agent's), weather-aware promises checked by simulation, and fitness functions that keep the design true.
environment: Python 3.12 (validated on 3.12.15, Linux x86_64) + numpy 2.5.3; reuses astronomy L300 #12 (ephem.py, Kasten & Young airmass), astronomy L100 #3 (timescales.py), simulation L200 #10 (ci()), kb/shared/local_agent (fake model server); optional Ollama + qwen2.5:1.5b for --real (pendingCi); astropy/astroplan cross-check pendingCi
overview: Eleven requests compete for 64 ten-minute dark slots at Gurgaon on 2026-11-19. Astronomy decides what is observable, simulation decides what a plan is worth under clouds, and a local model may only propose and explain. The interesting failures live at the seams between them, so every seam has a test.
prerequisites: astronomy L300 #12 Observation planning: airmass, twilight, Moon distance and a scheduler under constraints
astronomy L100 #3 Time systems: UTC, TAI, TT, Julian Date and sidereal time
simulation L200 #10 Warm-up, replications and confidence
ai-agents L400 #20 Deterministic core, LLM at the edge

glossary.meaning: Frozen wrapper of an aware datetime with UTC offset 0; the only time type sky maths accepts.
replace(tzinfo=...) attaches a zone without moving the clock; astimezone() moves the clock to the same instant in another zone.
Path length through the atmosphere relative to the zenith; 2.0 is reached near 30 deg altitude; infinite below the horizon here.
ok[i, s]: request i may start at slot s because every boundary of its block is dark, at airmass <= 2 and >= 30 deg from the Moon.
Probability that all n slots of a block are clear: pi_clear (1 - a)^(n-1) for the two-state Markov cloud chain.
Evaluate competing plans on the same simulated nights so their difference has low variance.
A boundary where one topic's output becomes another's input; the place integrated systems fail.

concepts: Type the time seam, then test it at the published instant.
Optimise the promise you can keep: expected value under weather.
Price every promise by simulation, paired by common random numbers.
Agents propose and explain; an independent validator decides.

designBrief.context: A 0.4 m robotic telescope at Gurgaon (28.46 N, 77.03 E, IST = UTC+05:30) has one night (2026-11-19, waxing gibbous Moon) and 11 observation requests with priorities 1-5 and uninterrupted exposures of 30-180 minutes. The site loses time to cloud spells. A local model is available to draft plans and explain them to observers.
constraints: no scheduled observation above airmass 2.0, below the horizon, outside astronomical darkness (Sun <= -18 deg) or within 30 deg of the Moon, re-checked every 5 minutes by an independent route
expected completed priority-weighted value >= 1.15 x the greedy baseline over 1000 seeded weather runs, with the paired 95 % CI of the difference above 0
the same seed gives the same schedule (plan hash) and the same weather runs
every promise (p_complete per block) within 3 binomial standard errors of its simulated completion rate
no plan from the local model is executed unless it passes the validator and promises at least the optimiser's value
designBrief.question: Which scheduler should run tonight, what may it promise each observer, and how do we stop a time-zone or agent mistake from pointing the telescope below the horizon?

architecture.summary: timeutil.UtcInstant is the only time that reaches sky.py, which turns astronomy L300 #12's ephemeris and Kasten & Young airmass into 64 ten-minute dark slots and a feasibility matrix. scheduler.py runs a greedy dispatcher and a seeded local search over request order (earliest-fit decoder) that maximises the expected value from weather.py's two-state Markov cloud model. validator.py re-derives altitude from astronomy L100 #3's apparent sidereal time every 5 minutes and judges every plan; weather.py replays 1000 nights with common random numbers to check the promises; agent_plan.py turns a local model's PLAN lines into typed rows for the same validator and gates its explanation. run_project.py prints one JSON line per milestone, seam and fitness function.

seams.contract: sky functions accept only UtcInstant (aware, offset 0, built by astimezone); local time exists only for display; sidereal time in hours, RA in degrees
seams.risk: a local wall clock read as UTC moves the sky 330 minutes: the scheduler's own airmass column still looks fine (1.982) while Betelgeuse is at -16.4 deg

seams.contract: model text -> 'PLAN <target> <ISO 8601 with Z or offset>' -> UtcInstant rows -> validator.validate(); adopt only with 0 violations and expected value >= the optimiser's; explanation numbers must be facts
seams.risk: an unzoned time is guessed, a below-horizon block is executed, or an invented number reaches an observer

seams.contract: the scheduler promises p_complete = pi (1 - a)^(n-1) per block and sum(priority x p) per plan; 1000 SeedSequence-child nights must reproduce both
seams.risk: nominal priority sums or independent-slot weather over-promise long blocks; an unpaired comparison hides a real difference in noise

seams.between: astronomy ↔ validator (units: degrees / hours / radians / minutes)
seams.contract: *_deg, *_h and *_min in names; LST hours x 15 -> degrees; radians only inside trig; exposures whole 10-min slots
seams.risk: a dropped x 15 or radians-as-degrees moves stars by tens of degrees without any exception

failureLab.inject: python run_project.py --inject local-as-utc (or SCHED_FAULT=local-as-utc): the scheduler hands the sky maths UtcInstant(slot.local.replace(tzinfo=None).replace(tzinfo=UTC)) - the IST wall clock relabelled as UTC. A bug that exists only because an astronomy library (UTC, Julian Date) meets a scheduler that thinks in local evenings.
failureLab.symptom: The scheduler is happy: its own rows report max airmass 1.982. The independent validator is not: 'Betelgeuse: altitude -16.4 deg, airmass inf at 2026-11-19T13:20:00Z'. Scorecard 7/12, exit 1 (M2, M3, M5, SEAM time, FF1 fail).
failureLab.diagnose: Compare sky_instant(slot) with slot.utc: they differ by exactly 330 minutes, the IST offset. The scheduler computed the sky 5 h 30 min after the instant it published. Type checks passed because a relabelled clock has offset 0.
failureLab.fix: Sky maths accepts only UtcInstant; build it with UtcInstant.from_aware() (astimezone), never replace(tzinfo=UTC); a lint-style test forbids that pattern outside the marked fault line; the seam test re-validates every block at its published UTC time by an independent sidereal route.
failureLab.test: labs/L600/05-observatory-scheduler/tests/test_obs_failure_lab.py (reproduces the fault) + labs/L600/05-observatory-scheduler/tests/test_obs_seam_time.py (fails with SCHED_FAULT=local-as-utc: 2 subtest failures; passes without)

buildTask.task: Agents write times many ways. Fix plan_times.parse_plan_time() (shipped UNFIXED: it relabels every time as UTC, so '+05:30' is shifted 330 minutes and a naive local time is silently accepted) so zoned times are converted to UtcInstant and anything without a zone raises ValueError.
buildTask.acceptance: BUILD_TARGET=mine python -m unittest tests.test_obs_build_task -v: shipped file 'Ran 5 tests ... FAILED (failures=3)'; after your fix 'OK'. BUILD_TARGET=mine python run_project.py then also passes M5 and SEAM agent (they fail on the shipped file).

scalingLimits: More requests, nights or telescopes: order search over requests x slots x sites loses quality and time; signal: the plan changes with the seed or the search stops improving long before its move budget. Move to ILP/CP (as Las Cumbres did) and keep the validator as the judge.
Real weather is not one stationary chain: realised completion rates fall outside the promised 3-sigma band night after night. Fit a and b per season from site logs and re-plan on live cloud data.

Low-precision ephemeris (J2000 without precession, about 0.36 deg by 2026; low-precision Moon): fine at airmass 2, not at a tight limit; signal: blocks within 0.5 deg of a limit disagree with astropy/astroplan (pendingCi).

codeWalkthrough.title: timeutil.UtcInstant
codeWalkthrough.detail: Frozen dataclass; __post_init__ refuses naive datetimes and non-zero offsets; from_aware() converts with astimezone(). lst_hours() reuses astronomy L100 #3's GAST.

codeWalkthrough.title: sky.feasibility()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Kasten & Young airmass and Moon separation at every 10-min boundary; ok[i, s] only if the whole block (n + 1 boundaries) passes. sky_instant() holds the injectable fault.

codeWalkthrough.title: scheduler.greedy()
codeWalkthrough.detail: At each free slot, the highest-priority feasible request (ties: airmass, name). Taking Deneb at dusk loses Vega - the myopia the local search fixes.

codeWalkthrough.title: scheduler.decode() + local_search()
codeWalkthrough.detail: An order becomes a plan by earliest fit; 3000 seeded swap/move proposals, accept if not worse, starting from greedy's order so the result is never below the baseline.

codeWalkthrough.title: weather.py
codeWalkthrough.detail: Two-state Markov clouds, one SeedSequence child per run, all-or-nothing blocks; expected() is the analytic promise, realised() the simulated payout, summary() the simulation topic's t-interval.

codeWalkthrough.title: validator.validate()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Independent sidereal route, 5-min samples, Sun, Moon, grid, overlap, duplicates; returns reasons and never repairs.

codeWalkthrough.title: agent_plan.py + run_project.py
codeWalkthrough.detail: Fake-model rules registered at runtime; PLAN lines parsed to UtcInstant; decide() adopts only a valid, at-least-as-good plan; explanations gated by numbers and names. run_project prints the scorecard and exits 1 on any FAIL.

troubleshooting.symptom: TypeError: sky maths needs a UtcInstant
troubleshooting.action: You passed a datetime or a JD; wrap it with UtcInstant.from_aware(dt) at the boundary, never inside sky.py.
The margin belongs to a workload: with little contention (try it 2) greedy is already optimal. Re-state the threshold in ADR 0002 rather than tuning the search to pass.
Check the model reply format (PLAN lines); a rejected plan is fine - M5 fails only if the valid offset-time plan is not adopted.

troubleshooting.symptom: Slow run (minutes) on a network drive
troubleshooting.action: Imports dominate; compute is about 2 s per build. Set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 or copy kb/ to a local disk.

agentAssist.task: A local model drafts tonight's plan as PLAN lines and explains the chosen plan's trade-offs in three sentences; code parses, validates, compares expected value and gates the explanation.
agentAssist.prompt: [[OBS-PLAN]] Propose tonight's observing plan, one line per block: PLAN <target> <start, ISO 8601 UTC>. <facts> site, dusk_utc, dawn_utc, requests (name priority exp_min), rules </facts>  |  [[OBS-EXPLAIN]] Explain the trade-offs of tonight's plan in 3 plain sentences. <facts> local_value, greedy_value, margin_pct, first_target, long_target, long_p </facts>

inRealSystems: Las Cumbres Observatory schedules its global telescope network from observation requests with an integer linear program (Lampoudi, Saunders & Eastman 2015) and re-schedules as conditions change.

astroplan (Astropy affiliated) expresses the same constraints (AtNightConstraint, AirmassConstraint, MoonSeparationConstraint) and offers sequential and priority schedulers - the library equivalent of sky.py + scheduler.py.
Weather generators in hydrology and agriculture use first-order two-state Markov chains for wet/dry occurrence since Gabriel & Neumann (1962).
useWhen: Use this shape whenever an optimiser plans against physical constraints and an uncertain environment and someone wants an AI to help: type the time and unit seams, judge every plan with an independent validator, price promises by simulation, and keep the model at the edge.
simulatorVsReal: No telescope or weather station: the sky comes from low-precision ephemerides (about 1-2 arcmin Sun/Moon, J2000 targets), clouds from an assumed Markov chain, and the agent from a deterministic fake model. A real deployment adds slews, filter changes, calibration frames, live cloud sensors and re-planning during the night.
caution: Planning and teaching only. Never let a model command hardware or bypass the validator; never put credentials, site network details or personal data in prompts. Weather parameters are assumptions - fit them to your site before promising anyone anything.
checkpoint: PASS: python run_project.py prints PASS 12/12 and exits 0; --inject local-as-utc exits 1 with SEAM time FAIL; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . reports 42 tests OK.

checkYourself.q: Why does a relabelled local time pass the UtcInstant type check?
checkYourself.a: replace(tzinfo=UTC) produces an aware datetime with offset 0 - a valid UtcInstant for the wrong instant. Only the independent re-validation at the published time catches it.

checkYourself.q: Why can the optimiser's mean advantage grow at a cloudier site while greedy wins more nights?
checkYourself.a: The optimiser avoids long risky blocks, which matters more when clouds are common (ratio 1.325), but the night-to-night spread also grows, so greedy's plan wins 23 % of single nights.

checkYourself.q: What stops an agent plan with a good-looking WHY line from being executed?
checkYourself.a: decide() never reads the WHY line: it parses PLAN lines into UtcInstant rows, runs the validator and compares expected value.

conceptSummary: A night scheduler where astronomy, simulation and an AI agent meet: typed UTC instants into sky maths, a weather-aware local search that beats greedy by 27 % over 1000 paired cloudy nights, promises checked by simulation, and a local model that proposes and explains while an independent validator decides.

macMini.gains: Real local models propose plans that only the validator can accept; astropy/astroplan and Stellarium check the sky maths independently; the INDI telescope and CCD simulators actually execute the night; and 100,000 Monte Carlo nights on every core test each completion promise far beyond the scorecard's 1,000.

experiments.title: A real model proposes tonight's plan; the validator decides
experiments.why: The fake makes one scripted mistake per class; a real model makes its own (zone-less times, overlaps, off-grid starts, invented targets, invented numbers). Each must be refused by code, and a plan is adopted only if it is valid and promises at least the optimiser's value.

steps.title: Fake baseline
steps.detail: agent_trials.py asks the plan and explanation prompts, then runs agent_plan.decide and checked_explanation.
steps.expected: adopted optimiser, violation_kinds {zone: 1, airmass: 3}, explanation_published true, no invented numbers.

steps.title: Real models
steps.detail: Models sized by mac_profile.py; one JSON line per model in ~/kb-runs/05-agent-trials.jsonl.
steps.expected: Most real plans refused; read which violation kind dominates (zone = prompt rule ignored, airmass/darkness = sky maths the model cannot do, unknown = invented targets). adopted agent only with agent_ok true and agent_value >= optimiser_value (exit 1 otherwise).

experiments.measure: Per model: violations by kind, adopted, explanation_published, invented_numbers.
experiments.decides: ADR-0004: if no model produces a valid plan, the agent's role narrows to explaining (proposals kept only as red-team input); if explanations fail the number gate, the deterministic fallback stays the default text.

experiments.title: Independent astronomy: astropy/astroplan and Stellarium
experiments.why: Both lab routes use J2000 coordinates without precession (up to ~0.36 deg per KNOWN-GAPS) and Vega's block reaches airmass 1.93 against the 2.0 limit; independent implementations measure how much that matters.

steps.title: astropy and astroplan numbers
steps.detail: Same samples (every 10 min of every block), same Kasten & Young airmass on both sides, no refraction (pressure 0).
steps.mac:
python3 -m pip install astropy astroplan
python3 astropy_check.py
steps.expected: max_dalt_deg of a few tenths of a degree (mostly precession), the largest airmass difference on the lowest block (Vega); ff1_violations_by_reference should be empty. The --here LST route gives 0.0019 deg.

steps.title: Stellarium numbers and picture
steps.detail: The .ssc script sets the site, freezes time and writes name,utc,altitude-geometric,altitude per sample with core.output.
steps.mac:
brew install --cask stellarium
python3 stellarium_export.py --out ~/kb-runs/05-plan.ssc
# Stellarium: F12 -> load -> run, then:
python3 stellarium_export.py --compare "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Stellarium/output.txt"
steps.expected: Each target centred and above the horizon at every sample; max_abs_dalt_deg comparable to astropy's; max_refraction_deg positive (refraction lowers airmass, so ignoring it is the safe side).

experiments.measure: Max |delta altitude| and |delta airmass| vs astropy and vs Stellarium; blocks whose reference airmass exceeds 2.0.
experiments.decides: FF1 margin and ADR-0001: a non-empty ff1_violations_by_reference means precess in sky.py or tighten the limit by the measured delta-airmass; otherwise KNOWN-GAPS records the measured bound instead of the 0.36 deg estimate.

experiments.title: INDI telescope + CCD simulators execute the plan
experiments.why: A plan is useful only if hardware can run it. The exporter drives INDI's simulators with INDI's own tools and standard properties, and exposes a new seam: J2000 in the scheduler, epoch of date (EQUATORIAL_EOD_COORD) at the mount.

steps.title: Dry run (works anywhere)
steps.detail: indi_export.py precesses each target (IAU 1976, tested on Meeus example 21.b) and writes CONNECTION, GEOGRAPHIC_COORD, ON_COORD_SET.TRACK, EQUATORIAL_EOD_COORD.RA;DEC (hours; degrees; atomic), CCD_EXPOSURE and TELESCOPE_PARK commands with busy-then-Ok waits (indi_eval -w).
steps.expected: 39 commands for the 5-block plan; RA in hours in [0, 24); J2000-to-JNow shifts of 0.09-0.37 deg for these targets (--no-precess shows the unprecessed pointing).

steps.title: Execute against the simulators
steps.detail: Start indiserver with both simulators (native build, or a Debian container with indi-bin), then run the script; KStars/Ekos can watch the same server.
steps.mac:
indiserver -v indi_simulator_telescope indi_simulator_ccd &
bash ~/kb-runs/05-night-indi.sh
indi_getprop "Telescope Simulator.EQUATORIAL_EOD_COORD.*"
steps.expected: Per block: TRACK on, goto, slew reaches Ok, one exposure reaches Ok; finally PARK and 'plan executed'. An indi_eval timeout stops the script (set -e) - the behaviour a robotic observatory needs.

experiments.measure: Blocks executed / planned; slew seconds per block; pointing error between commanded JNow and the mount's EQUATORIAL_EOD_COORD.
experiments.decides: ADR-0001 gains a coordinate-epoch rule (J2000 inside, epoch of date only at the INDI boundary, precession test as its seam test); measured slew times replace the implicit zero-slew assumption (a transition time per block if they exceed one 10-minute slot).

macMini.overnight: caffeinate -i python3 weather_overnight.py --nights 100000: both plans over 100,000 Markov-weather nights (P_CLEAR_TO_CLOUD 0.02 / 0.04 / 0.08) on every performance core. It reveals each block's observed completion against its promise (z scores that 1,000 nights cannot resolve), the tail risk P(value = 0), and whether FF2 (optimised >= 1.15 x greedy) survives a site cloudier or clearer than assumed (ADR-0003).

validation.here: Linux sandbox, Python 3.12.15, numpy 2.5.3: mac_mini/tests (16 tests OK) - precession vs Meeus example 21.b, INDI command set/atomic RA;DEC/bash -n, J2000-as-JNow seam, realtime block filling, execute-without-INDI skip, LST reference route (max 0.0019 deg), forced FF1 violation, astropy-missing skip, Stellarium script and compare on synthetic output, Monte Carlo chunks equal one matrix and 1 vs 2 workers identical, fake-model trial; weather_overnight --here (2,000 nights: ratio 1.25 / 1.26 / 1.31), agent_trials --here, indi_export --here ran; checks_05_mac.py OK.
